subject: Discovery recap: Reliability & graceful degradation (FinPay)
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@finpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: Reliability & graceful degradation (FinPay)

Alicia - thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap of what we heard, the success criteria you gave, and proposed next steps. Please confirm or correct anything I missed.

Pain points we heard:
- Recent production incidents (Dec 2025 & Mar 2026) where the primary model endpoint spiked latency >5x; customer-facing failures lasted ~20-30 minutes.
- Lack of automated fallbacks - traffic queued or errored instead of failing over to a smaller/compatible model variant or another region.
- Difficulty getting clear token-level cost/latency breakdowns for specific routes.

Current stack (from call):
- Inference hosted in GCP us-central1.
- Primary model: finance-bert-v2 (proprietary), currently self-hosted on TPU instances with autoscaling.
- Some routing done at LB level; no per-model canary or automatic model variant fallback.

Success criteria (what matters to FinPay):
- End-to-end SLO: 99.9% p95 latency <= 300ms for core routing (internal goal).
- Graceful degradation: when primary model fails or is overloaded, failover to a cheaper/quantized variant with degraded but acceptable accuracy, or route to a sibling region within 60s.
- Observable incident timelines with token-level cost and latency attribution so ops can triage quickly.

Risks / constraints:
- Regulated data flows require audit logs and KMS-managed keys - you mentioned compliance team needs SOC2 evidence.
- Procurement prefers a single contract for hosted + dedicated if we require reserved capacity.

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive with your infra team (60 mins) to validate model variants and KV cache integration - suggested attendees: Evan (infra), your SRE, our Runtime lead (Marissa).
2) Share historical incident timeline (you mentioned a spreadsheet) and we'll map recommended fallback configs and expected cost delta.
3) Draft a mutual action plan & high-level SLA options for your security and procurement teams.

I attached the FinPay incident template (fill in gaps) and a first-pass SLA redline for convenience.

Would next Tue (May 12) 10-11am PT work for the technical deep-dive?

Thanks,
Jonas
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0132

Attachments: SLA-redlines.pdf, FinPay-incident-summary-2025-2026.xlsx

From: Alicia Gomez <alicia@finpay.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evan Park <evan.park@finpay.com>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Reliability & graceful degradation (FinPay)

Thanks Jonas - this is a great summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Incident history: the spreadsheet (attached) has the two incidents you called out plus a minor one in Feb. The Dec incident was caused by a sudden spike in request size; March was an autoscaler misconfiguration that led to thrashing.

2) Priority: reliability > cost for the first quarter. We need a graded escalation path so customer-impacting requests never time out for more than ~2-3 minutes.

3) Fallbacks: ideally we have 2 fallback tiers - a quantized variant (lower accuracy) and a regional failover. Regional failover has policy constraints (data residency) for a subset of customers; we'll flag those.

Would be useful if your MR could sketch expected RTO/RPO for the two fallback tiers and a cost delta (ballpark). Tech deep-dive Tue 5/12 10am PT works for Evan and me.

-Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Head of Product, FinPay
alicia@finpay.com

On Sun, May 10, 2026 at 2:05 PM Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Alicia - thanks again for taking the time today....

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@finpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Evan Park <evan.park@finpay.com>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 08:49:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Reliability & graceful degradation (FinPay)

Perfect - thanks for the quick reply and for confirming the time. A few quick answers inline and a short prep ask for the deep-dive: 

Inline:
- RTO/RPO: for a model-variant fallback (same region): RTO ~ 30-90s depending on model size and cache warm-up; for regional failover (different region), RTO ~ 60-180s depending on data residency checks and KV cache repopulation. We'll give more precise numbers after we see your traffic profiles.
- Cost delta: rough estimate - quantized variant ~20-40% lower per-token cost; regional failover depends on inter-region egress and sizing but expect +10-30% on top of baseline for duplicated capacity when hot standby is used.

Prep asks for Tue deep-dive:
- Evan: send a sanitized slice of the March incident logs and the autoscaler config (we only need scalars and timings).
- Alicia: flag the percentage of traffic that is data-residency restricted (approximate OK).
- From our side Marissa (runtime) will bring recommended fallback configs (per-model policies, canary window, automatic rollback triggers) and Rishi (customer success) will bring SLA options for procurement.

Also attaching a short one-page: "Graceful Degradation Patterns" that outlines the model variants + routing strategies we typically recommend.

See you Tue 10am PT - sending calendar invite now.

Jonas
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: graceful-degradation-patterns.pdf

- March incident runbook entry included: surge at 15:32, primary model OOM at 15:34, autoscaler created 4 new instances but LB drained traffic slowly leading to a 22-minute degradation window.
- For residency-sensitive customers ~12% of total traffic.
- We can join the call with our SRE (Priya) if helpful.

Evan
